about: Every third-party component Nollie installs or builds, pinned by version and checksum. Change a pin here first, then run python3 Tools/dev/check-latest.py --local to find each place that has to follow. python3 Tools/dev/check-latest.py reports which pins are behind upstream; it never changes anything.

components.name: uv by Astral
components.role: Download manager for the Mac setup
components.notes: Notarized by Astral (team 2DC432GLL2, identifier sh.astral.uv). A firewall that allows apps by signing identity sees it as new: 0.13.1 was uv-12607afb3fd970b7.

components.name: Python (python-build-standalone)
components.role: Nollie's own Python, separate from any Python on the Mac
components.notes: uv installs it and checks it against the checksum built into uv, so this pin moves with uv. The artifact here is for reference and the dry run; it matches the release's SHA256SUMS.

components.name: Hermes Agent by Nous Research
components.notes: v0.23.1 is the tag's own commit. 0.23 moved new-bot setup into hermes_cli/profiles_initialization.py and replaced the browser_* tools with browser_exec.

components.name: Hermes's Python packages
components.role: The libraries Hermes needs, from Hermes's own lockfile
components.notes: Installed with uv sync --frozen --no-build: every wheel is checked against the hash in the lockfile, which is inside the pinned Hermes archive.

components.name: Trafilatura, pypdf and their dependencies
components.notes: Hash-locked for macOS on Apple silicon and Python 3.14; installed with --require-hashes and wheels only.

components.name: Cua Driver by Cua AI, built as Nollie Computer
components.role: Lets a bot use approved apps on this Mac (Direct edition)
components.notes: Built from source by Tools/computer-helper/build-driver.sh; the tree ids, Cargo.lock and binary checksums live in pin.env.

components.name: Rust toolchain
components.notes: Whatever the pinned Cua Driver's rust-toolchain.toml names.

components.name: Sparkle
components.role: Updates the Direct Mac edition by itself
components.license: MIT (with a few BSD-style and zlib-style notices for bundled parts)
components.notes: The release file Sparkle's own Swift package points at (its Package.swift carries this checksum). Only the Direct Mac edition links and embeds it, so it is fetched and checked by Tools/sparkle/fetch-sparkle.sh and linked by build settings rather than as a package product, which would link into the App Store edition too. It also holds the key, signing and appcast tools the release uses.
